raw_extraction.source_limitations: All information is derived from a research context and does not constitute clinical guidance or medical approval. No efficacy, dosage, contraindications, or diagnostic thresholds are established. Findings are observational and hypotheses, not proven causation. The studies are part of ongoing research and not operational recommendations for human health in spaceflight.

entities.description: A study monitoring astronauts' well-being, activity, and sleep patterns during Artemis II to understand human health and performance in deep space.
entities.evidence_text: A study on Artemis II monitored astronauts' well-being, activity, and sleep patterns to learn more about human health and performance in deep space.

entities.description: Analysis of blood and saliva samples to assess immune system changes due to deep space exposure.
entities.evidence_text: Scientists analyzed blood and saliva samples from Artemis II crew members to see how deep space changes the immune system.

entities.description: A consistent set of health data collected by crew to support future research on astronaut health.
entities.evidence_text: Crews supplied a consistent set of health information to a data bank so that future researchers can learn more about astronaut health.

entities.description: A daily B vitamin supplement study to prevent or mitigate brain and eye changes in space.
entities.evidence_text: Investigating if a daily B vitamin supplement can prevent or mitigate brain and eye changes that may affect some humans in space

entities.description: Study of skull fluid pressure and its relationship to eye and brain changes in astronauts.
entities.evidence_text: Examining the relationship between fluid pressure inside the skull and changes to the eyes and brain of astronauts

entities.description: A suite of studies examining multiple body systems to understand human body changes in orbit.
entities.evidence_text: Providing a better understand of how the human body changes while orbiting the Earth via a suite of studies examining multiple body systems

entities.canonical_name: Simulating Manual Piloting for Moon Landings
entities.description: Study on how gravity transitions impact astronaut piloting capabilities for Moon landings.
entities.evidence_text: Assessing how gravity transitions may affect the piloting capabilities of astronauts for future Moon landings

entities.description: Assessment of crew discomfort during re-entry and integration with spacecraft sensor data.
entities.evidence_text: Surveying crew members' potential discomfort during re-entry to Earth and combining it with sensor data on spacecraft

entities.description: Detection of substances in spinal fluid linked to space-related brain and eye changes.
entities.evidence_text: Detecting substances in the spinal fluid of astronauts associated with space-related brain and eye changes

entities.description: Consistent physiological and psychological measurements to understand spaceflight effects on crew.
entities.evidence_text: Collecting a consistent set of physiological and psychological measurements to better understand how spaceflight affects the bodies and minds of crew members

entities.description: Testing tight thigh cuffs to retain bodily fluids in legs and prevent eye disorders in space.
entities.evidence_text: Testing if wearing tight thigh cuffs could keep more bodily fluids in the legs to help determine if future strategies can avert the eye disorders that can develop in space

entities.description: Study of physical differences affecting blood flow and coagulation in space.
entities.evidence_text: Examining physical differences in astronauts that may contribute to blood flow and blood coagulation changes in space

entities.description: Study of exercise in space without a treadmill on human health and performance.
entities.evidence_text: Examining how exercise in space without a treadmill affects human health and performance

record.evidence_text: Scientists analyzed blood and saliva samples from Artemis II crew members to see how deep space changes the immune system.
